items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: When Zoot Sims pointed at me, on a bandstand, my father was looking at Zoot like, “no, not the kid, don’t point at him.”

ctx.x: Do you think that stuff is good?

I couldn’t tell you a thing about it. And I think the way that I learned it was when you listen to George Barnes play, he knew the chords to the songs. And when I learned, the best thing that I learned was knowing the chords to the songs first. Because my father wouldn’t let me play a solo for a year. I just played the chords. So when I went back to blow on the songs I already knew, ah, it’s E flat minor 7 is the first chord, A flat, D flat, G flat, okay. So at least I could go [scats]. I mean I could know where…

how you’re going to play on a song, or what your style is going to be. And then I think it’s the same thing like the books, leave all that stuff at home. And once you’re on the bandstand you’re going to see where all that’s going to work. And I think it’s just learn by doing. The more I’ve been playing with the group, the more that you realize your ass is on the line every night, you know it’s almost like blowing by fear. You know? It’s your turn. When Zoot Sims pointed at me, on a bandstand, my father was…
